I have uploaded a larger version of text, but just in case:

CURRENT STRUCTURE

In mirroring Reddit, the idea of content in a voting system has its ups and downs. It allows for a user influenced order - which is welcomed as a portion of fair ground without the need for curation (aside from moderation). It is indeed effective but considering how we have the desire to leave reddit due to it’s flaws, we cannot create a new system based on the old without running into these same problems.

This leads to finding a new solution that delivers the essence of what Reddit was truly about - delivering content from around the web with a community interaction.

INTRO TO UNIVERSES

Delivering content is key. The internet has become a place that is so vast, that it truly is a collection of universes. Some share similarities, while others tend to keep their distance. Regardless, trying to map out such a complex system does require something a computer cannot do.

THE HUMAN ASPECT

Human curated content is something that allows people to connect not on a processing level, but on a relating level. This is utilizing aspects such as feelings and experiences to help shape how we intend to collect content. For example, take it this way: For those of you who have used Pandora, it is great for listening to music but you are dealing with curated music that is not only predictable, but is based on mainstream influences. Now if you switched over to another music service such as 8tracks, this drastically changes the game by offering a user to create their own playlist and share with others. This opened up the possibility to have music discovery based on the individual experience. You use the power of creation to add experiences to others, resulting in inspiration, discovery, and a music playlist that is ultimately more worthwhile. Obviously some people will have better tastes than others, no different from people existing with different views around the world.

Now this same concept can be taken for content found on the internet. For those who were RSS savvy, we held a place in our heart for Google Reader. It allowed us to curate content from all aspects of the web in one convenient place. It was limited in features but it still delivered. Since it’s departure, there have been many ‘fill-in’ sites such as Feedly (which seems to be the better of options without a charge) but for any power user, there hasn’t been anything that has filled the gap with what Google Reader offered the internet.

UNIVERSES

What I have shared previously is the concept of UNIVERSES. This would be my answer in allowing a new way to curate and discover content. If we take the core concepts of what made Reddit Reddit, mixed with the desire to customize and self curate your own collections, it could result in a new form of discovery that the internet could use. The system itself would no longer support the old structure the reddit has made popular. Instead, the system I suggest would replace the old, while still being able to emulate the Reddit structure. With a new system, it can also introduce content based on a feed building aspect, which will allow for flexible innovations.

Currently, the structure is based on a user submitted aspect mixed with a voter influence. To have a structure that is feed based, the parameters would focus on ordering the content based on context. This means that one can refine the feed to appear in order of choice. With the right refined options, you could easily order the feed to emulate Reddit by allowing it to sort by voting while also constraining the time span you would like to see. So one can still manage a Verse no differently then they do today, but would also offer more options so that a ‘viewer’ can dictate how the content appears.

Subverses would still exist in the same aspect thus allowing for a place to submit and share content. What is introduced are UNIVERSES - which are collections of content. You are able to pick and chose, or even automate the content to be the created custom feed. This could import a whole subverse, allow for a user to build up custom folders for any given subverse. Some may find this example similar to how Multreddits were handled.

What sets this system apart though is that lets say there was a specific post/link in a subverse and you wanted to put that into a UNIVERSE, well you can. You can even choose to import external feeds with the right infrastructure. Meaning you can integrate RSS on a whole other scale. With the desire to build externally, you are able to share content from a specific source directly to a subverse from a UNIVERSE. This will also offer a great tracking system to see where else the link was shared or curated on Whoaverse. Of course a given subverse will allow for it’s own comment & voting. If you have been able to keep up so far, you can see that the subverse and universe share a similar structure but run parallel to each other.

The subverses would still exist with their /v/ link structure while UNIVERSES would carry a link structured based on the user. With a userbase that is structured for no repetitive username creation, this will self organize so that there will be no errors. The naming of the UNIVERSES will also have to carry a structure per user so that they cannot name two UNIVERSES with the same exact title. For this case, I feel that a naming system would automatically add a # to set it apart if you were to create a UNIVERSE that already has the given name. This will hold a same edit functionality seen in comments.
